_about: X.25 conformance vectors shared by the C# stack (RetroIO) and the C emulator (x25emu).
Every vector names the clause it was read from. Text sources: E:\Dev\RCL\Specs\X25 -
T-REC-X.25-199610-I (10/96) unless another document is named. Packet type identifier values
were cross-checked between the C# builder and the C header src/x25/x25.h because the
pdftotext rendering of Table 5-2 is unreadable; both agree and both have been seen on the wire.
status: 'pass' = must pass today and always. 'knownFail:<rule>' = documents a defect the code
has TODAY (rule numbers are from Migration/X25 one-stack plan.md section 3); the reader asserts
that the vector still FAILS, so a fix shows up as a red test that somebody must read and flip.
Never change a vector's expectation to make a test green - change the code or the status.

facilityDecode.spec: X.25 7.3.1.1, 7.3.1.2: log2 packet size in bits 4-1; window in bits 7-1; first octet = from called, second = from calling
X.25 7.3.1.2; packet size absent -> network default 128 (7.3.1.1 'All Administrations will provide a packet size of 128')
X.25 7.1 Table 7-1: class D (bits 8,7 = 11) has a length octet; 7.3.7 NUI 0xC6 is class D. Unknown facility is stepped over by its declared length and kept for pass-through
facilityDecode.note: window decodes right today; the pass-through field does not exist yet, so the vector fails on passThroughHex

facilityDecode.spec: X.25 7.1: marker = code 0x00 + parameter 0x00 separates X.25 facilities from non-X.25 network facilities; everything after it is NOT an X.25 facility
facilityDecode.note: today the second 42 0A 0A is read as packet size 1024 (audit F-01-01 twin)

facilityDecode.spec: X.25 7.1: marker parameter all ones precedes facilities for the called DTE's network
X.25 7.1: marker parameter 00001111 precedes ITU-T-specified DTE facilities (Annex G), passed unchanged
X.25 7.1: code 0xFF is the extension; the NEXT octet is an extended code with class from its own bits 8,7. Extended 0x42 is class B (2 octets) and is NOT packet size
facilityDecode.note: today 0xFF is treated as class D with 0x42 as its length (audit F-01-02 twin)

addresses.spec: X.25 5.2.2.2: bits 4-1 = called length in semi-octets, bits 8-5 = calling length; digits BCD, high digit in bits 8-5
X.25 5.2.2.2: calling starts on the semi-octet after called; odd total -> a zero semi-octet is inserted after the calling address
X.25 5.2.2.2: the length field is four bits, so 15 digits is the maximum in the non-TOA/NPI format
X.25 5.2.2.2: 16 semi-octets cannot be expressed in a four-bit length field
addresses.note: today the length is masked with 0x0F and becomes 0 while all 16 digits are still written (audit F-01-07 twin, bounded)

addresses.spec: X.25 5.2.2.2: addresses are decimal digits coded in BCD
addresses.note: today 'A' - '0' = 17 is written as a nibble

packets.spec: X.25 5.2.2 Figure 5-x: GFI 0001 + LCGN, LCN, PTI 00001011, address block, facility length, facilities, CUD
X.25 5.2.3: PTI 00001111; address block then facility length and facilities
packets.note: X.25 5.2.3.1.2: 'The use of the called and calling DTE address length fields in call accepted packets is only mandatory when the called DTE address field, the calling DTE address field or the facility length field is present.' Today the C# builder omits that octet (writes 10 01 0F 06 ...) so the facility length lands where the address lengths belong. The C emulator's x25_accept (src/x25/x25.c) writes the address block before the facility length, as the spec requires.

X.25 5.1.2: the GFI is bits 8-5, so the logical channel group number is bits 4-1 (four bits, 0..15) and LCN runs 0..4095. The C# builder and parser mask the group with 0x07 (X25PacketBuilder.GFI.LCG_MASK), so LCN 4095 is built as 17 FF (LCN 2047) and 1F FF parses back as 2047. Every LCN from 2048 up is corrupted in both directions.

X.25 5.4.2.1: PTI 00100011, 1 to 32 octets of user data
X.25 5.6: LCGN/LCN zero, PTI 11110001, diagnostic code, diagnostic explanation
